requirements.requirement: Run the Node.js application on node1 in a rootless Podman container under the nodeapp service account, with both the container and service named node-hello.
requirements.summary: Post-reboot observations show rootless Podman, an active node-hello.service, a running node-hello container executing node /app/server.js, and its host-side process owned by nodeapp.

requirements.requirement: Return exactly Hello, world! from / on TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: File-based comparisons before and after reboot matched exactly 13 bytes, Hello, world!, over the node address on port 8080. The recovered listener is bound to 0.0.0.0:8080.

requirements.requirement: Start without requiring an interactive login.
requirements.summary: nodeapp uses /usr/sbin/nologin, lingering is enabled, and the generated service is linked into the user default target. A bounded full-node restart changed the boot ID and directly demonstrated automatic recovery of the service, rootless container, listener, firewall state, and exact HTTP response.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The sole managed node also has complete provider-wide restart evidence: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different independently corroborated post-restart boot identity, and recovered service, container, network exposure, and exact application behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation is evidenced. The observed mutations—installing Podman, creating nodeapp and enabling linger, creating and building the application and Quadlet, starting the service, opening the required port, and performing the mandatory restart—each had a clear task or verification role. The failed enable attempt showed no retained change. Temporary response files were trap-cleaned, final package health was sound, no failed services appeared, and the only material new listener was the intended port 8080 service.
